name: Solar Polysilicon, Ingot & Wafer: India's Missing Upstream Link
scope: India has 200+ GW of module and ~30 GW of cell capacity but imports nearly all polysilicon, ingots and wafers from China; MNRE's ALMM List-III makes domestic wafers mandatory from 1 Jun 2028 and a capex/PLI subsidy for polysilicon was reported under consideration in Aug-Sep 2026, so listed module/cell makers are board-approving multi-thousand-crore ingot-wafer capex -- PARTLY DISCOVERED already (Waaree, Premier, Tata Power get heavy coverage) while the smaller names (Vikram Solar, Saatvik, Websol) and the polysilicon leg are earlier; verify re-rating before acting.
questions: What is the solar polysilicon-ingot-wafer value chain, and how dependent is India on Chinese supply today (share of imports, current ~2 GW operational ingot/wafer capacity vs ~30 GW pipeline)?

What exactly does MNRE's ALMM List-III (wafers/ingots, effective 1 June 2028, conditional on 15 GW across 3+ independent units) require, and what is the status of the proposed polysilicon capex/PLI subsidy (size, eligibility, timing)?

What have Waaree Energies, Premier Energies, Tata Power, Vikram Solar, Saatvik Green Energy and Websol Energy each formally announced (capacity in GW, capex in Rs crore, location, partners, commissioning timeline), with exchange-filing or investor-presentation sources?

Are there other listed companies (e.g. Emmvee, Solex, Insolation, Reliance, Adani Enterprises, equipment or materials suppliers such as ASM Technologies) with confirmed ingot/wafer/polysilicon plans, and which are only 'evaluating'?

Which listed companies could supply upstream inputs and equipment (metallurgical-grade silicon, quartz crucibles, graphite thermal fields, diamond wire, crystal pullers) and is there company-confirmed involvement?

How do unit economics look: Rs ~850 cr/GW polysilicon capex, wafer price collapse, Chinese overcapacity, US minimum import prices on polysilicon/wafers -- can Indian wafers be cost-competitive without protection?

How well does each company's balance sheet support the capex (Waaree ~Rs 6,200 cr, Premier ~Rs 6,000 cr, Tata Power ~Rs 6,500 cr, Vikram 9 GW) -- funding mix, dilution, debt, and execution track record in the new technology?

How much has the market already priced in: 6- and 12-month share-price moves of each name, valuation vs peers, and how much broker/mainstream media coverage groups these names as an 'ingot-wafer' theme?
Which size tier offers the earliest, least-discovered exposure (small/mid caps vs large caps where solar is one segment), and which names have the highest share of revenue exposed to this theme?

What are the key risks and catalysts: subsidy announcement, ALMM-III notification milestones and any deferral, first commissioning dates, technology (TOPCon/back-contact) shifts, Chinese price dumping, DCR demand and anti-dumping duties?

integrated_cell_module_makers: Listed module/cell manufacturers with announced ingot-wafer capex (largest scale, most covered)
emerging_midsmall_caps: Smaller solar makers building backward integration
Small/mid caps with stated ingot-wafer plans or MoUs, earlier in the cycle and less covered
power_utility_entrants: Large diversified groups adding an ingot-wafer plant to captive solar supply chains
